liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): The transition into I Know You Rider is described as flawless and smoky; The sequence is awesome, featuring a sick note-bending solo by Jerry [18][25]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): An early rendition of the song drips nicely into Comes A Time; Phil hits the brakes hard on the segue, but the wah-wah exit to Estimated is smooth [18][26]
- **Comes A Time** (2 reviews): Jerry struggles a little with the breakout, but delivers a cool solo; One of the most gorgeous readings, with Jerry's lilting voice and masterful feedback control [25][26]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Features great guitar playing, with the reviewer crediting Jerry Garcia for the performance [18]
- **Minglewood Blues** (1 review): A rowdy opener with a fired-up Jerry sets the tone for the evening [20]
- The show features tight, really great versions of Uncle John's Band, He's Gone, and Sugar Magnolia [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-10.132518.aud.nak700.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 171 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd80-05-10.rolfe.vernon.18158.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 4.4/5 by 20 [4]. Said about its sound: The recording is loud, unrefined, and Garcia's voice sounds distant, limiting the quality rating; The sound is quite good after some equalizer adjustments; Sound quality is not great, though the show itself is described as really hot [19][20][22]
- **gd1980-05-10.aud.wise.83063.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 23 songs; 173 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [5]
- **gd1980-05-10.aud.willy.7559.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 172 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [6]
- **gd1980-05-10.152806.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 175 min [7]

## Around the show

- Firecrackers went off, and the Hartford crowd was psyched up, energizing the band [20]
- M80s exploded sporadically throughout the show, causing confusion and laughter among attendees [22]
- Before the show, the group hung out in a Hartford park with blooming trees, playing frisbee [23]
- Startling M80s went off sporadically through the whole show, affecting the listening experience [27]
- Several loud bangs, remembered as firecrackers, occurred during the show, causing the crowd to boo [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-10.132518.aud.nak700.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: flac16/48kHz ; Cassette Audience Master recorded By Jim Wise (patched out of Jeff Hellman); Nakamichi CM-700 Electret Condenser Microphones w/ CP-4 Shotgun… [1]
- **gd80-05-10.rolfe.vernon.18158.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [4]. Also: The reviewer doubts this is the master tape, noting it has been stepped on too many times [22]
- **gd1980-05-10.aud.wise.83063.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Andrew F.; source: Three Nakamichi CM-300's > patched thru Nakamichi 550 > Sony TC-D5 [5]. Also: Mics were on a stand next to the soundboard, from the same MAC as ShnID-7559; This is an excellent transfer from the MAC, a major improvement over the clipped 7559; Tape flips in the second set were patched with material from Steve Rolfe's tape [5]
- **gd1980-05-10.aud.willy.7559.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Willy; source: Nak 300's > Sony D5 [6]. Also: Dropouts occur between 11:26 and 11:31 in He's Gone on disc two, tape six [6]
- **gd1980-05-10.152806.senn.blend.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Recorded, Transferred and Mastered by Rob Eaton; transferred by Mastered by Scott Clugston April 2021; source: Rob Eaton's Master Audience Cassettes; (2)Sennheiser 441 mics (Left + Right) + (1) Sennheiser 421 mic (Center) blend > Nakamichi 550 [7]. Also: Rob Eaton provided the master recording, transfer, and hard drive for this blend; Nakamichi 700 source supplies patches in Jam, Drums, and Alabama Getaway [7]
